snippet: Lamport proved that no agreement can be reached in an asynchronous network with even one crash failure under the FLP impossibility theorem.
relevance_reason: Defines Byzantine Fault Tolerance on Page 1

snippet: Lamport Logical Clocks assign a monotonically increasing integer timestamp C(e) to every event. If event a happens before b within the same process, C(a) < C(b). The receiver updates its clock to max(C(receive), C(send)) + 1.

Raft decomposes consensus into three independent subproblems: Leader Election, Log Replication, and Safety. If a follower receives no communication over an election timeout, it transitions to Candidate and requests votes via RequestVote RPCs.
relevance_reason: Defines Raft Consensus Protocol on Page 3

snippet: Classic Multi-Paxos reaches consensus across distinct log slots through two-phase rounds: Phase 1 Prepare and Promise, and Phase 2 Accept and Accepted.
relevance_reason: Defines Paxos State Machine Replication on Page 4

snippet: Brewer CAP Theorem states that any distributed data store can simultaneously provide at most two of three guarantees: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance.
Amazon Dynamo adopts an AP model using consistent hashing, vector clocks for versioning, and anti-entropy background synchronization using Merkle trees via gossip protocols.
relevance_reason: Defines DynamoDB Gossip Protocol on Page 6

snippet: MapReduce coordinates master and worker nodes where Mappers partition intermediate keys using hash mod R and Reducers aggregate sorted keys.
Apache Spark introduces Resilient Distributed Datasets (RDDs) with deterministic lineage graphs enabling in-memory fault tolerance without disk spills.
